ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic lung cancer to the heart

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with cardiac and oncologic history
salient_findings: ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Progressive dyspnea on exertion
History of multiple prior cardiac events
History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
Received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery 10 months prior
Denies chest pain
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level was 40 ng/L
ECG shows normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3
Transthoracic echocardiogram shows well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum
Preserved left ventricular systolic function
No regional wall motion abnormalities
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade
Coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and imaging studies show a large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade, which is consistent with malignant pericardial effusion.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of impending cardiac tamponade, this is a symptom rather than a diagnosis, and the underlying cause is more likely malignant pericardial effusion given the patient's history of cancer.

rejected.label: Metastatic lung cancer to the heart
rejected.why: This option is too broad and does not specifically explain the pericardial effusion and impending tamponade.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of inflammation or infection to support this diagnosis, and the patient's history of cancer is a more likely explanation for the findings.

rejected.label: Cardiac metastasis from brain cancer
rejected.why: The patient's brain cancer is not the primary cancer, and the history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the myocardium makes it more likely that the cardiac involvement is due to the lung cancer.
